data.narrative:
Copenhagen Atomics is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a typical 2.0x multiplier for Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $50M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—yields a median implied value of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneous technology maturity, capital intensity, and regulatory pathway assumptions across the nuclear energy subsector.

The two methods produce a triangulated range of $42M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $429M. This wide band reflects material uncertainty around Copenhagen Atomics' technical differentiation relative to peers, commercialization timeline, and the ongoing fragmentation in private nuclear valuations. Stage-progression suggests conservatism; peer-median reflects the sector's current elevated multiples. Key uncertainties include regulatory de-risking trajectory and capital requirements to demonstration phase.
